title: With snowshoes on, you can walk across deep snow that would swallow your boots
alt: A packed snow trail runs up a wide snowy valley between rocky peaks under a blue sky; one walker with poles and a backpack is a small figure on the trail.

posts.facebook:
Picture walking on top of deep snow, not sinking into it. Snowshoes spread your weight, so you stay on the surface. That opens up winter landscapes you could not walk through in boots.

In several US national parks, including Crater Lake in Oregon and Bryce Canyon in Utah, a park ranger (one of the park's own guides) will lend you snowshoes and lead the walk for free. Crater Lake charges a winter entrance fee of $20 per vehicle. No experience is needed. In Scotland, you can book a guided snowshoe day in the Cairngorms, a range of mountains there.

It's hard work. Bryce Canyon calls snowshoeing highly strenuous, which means very tiring. Wear warm layers and waterproof boots, and bring water. Walks can be cancelled if there is too little snow or the weather is severe.

Would you give it a try?
